text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG

- Bonn coalition sticks to its gold revalutaion plan. Coalition leaders say European currency union will not be delayed. The liberal Free Democrats will not give into tax rises to help Germany plug budget gaps
- Bundesbank stands by the Maastricht Treaty. Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer does not want a delay in the launch of the euro

- The Bonn coalition appears to be chipping away at the foundation of its alliance. Finance Minister Theo Waigel is at the centre of confusion as coalition contemplates plans to revalue gold and some coalition partners calls for a rise in fuel tax to help budget gaps
HANDELSBLATT
- The sister party of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats, the Bavarian Christian Social Union, want a step-by-step plan for revaluation of gold
- Bonn wants to protect savings banks
- Berlin municipal government crisis is over after Christian Demcorats and Social Democrats agree to continue coalition until election in 1999
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG

- Free Democrat (FDP) politicians threaten to leave the coalition if other members of the coalition try to raise taxes. FDP party leader Wolfgang Gerhard says solidarity surcharge, levied to fund reconstruction of east Germany, should be cut as planned -- over new talks about consolidating the budget
- Interior Minister Manfred kanther's exaggerated warning. The situation shows now increase in organised crime
- German Justice Minister Edzard Schmidt-Jortzig rejects brain death as moment of death
- Labour Minister Norbert Bluem says compromise on pensions is impossible with the opposition Social Demcrats
- Row over possibility that Germany will go ahead with raising fuel taxes without consulting auto industry
- Talks about revaluation of central bank gold continue
DIE WELT
- Coalition stands before test of whether it can stay together. Liberal Free Democrats reject tax hikes and opposition Social Democrat leader Oskar Lafontaine calls for new elections
- 20,000 celebrate Bayern Munich's victory
- Germany's reputation runs into danger. Experts see the credibility of their finance policy at risk over gold revaluation plans
- Head of economic institute in Halle, Ruediger Pohl, says Finance Minister Theo Waigel's euro plans have not gone off the rails
- Head of the federal office for Post and Telecommunications, Hans Gottfried Bernrath, says Waigel faces a budgetary dilemma, but that the sale of Telekom shares is possible and a good idea
